nodes.title: Name the tabs with a union type
nodes.why: TabId lists the three valid selections, so selectTab and isActive accept nothing else and a misspelled id fails type checking.
nodes.alternative: Use plain strings or numeric indexes for tab ids.
nodes.tradeoff: Adding a tab means extending the union as well as the template, which is also what keeps the two in step.

nodes.title: Use one typed active-tab signal
nodes.why: A single TabId signal drives active classes, aria-selected and panel visibility, so the three can never disagree.
nodes.alternative: Maintain a separate boolean for each tab and panel.
nodes.tradeoff: One value cannot describe two open panels, which is exactly the constraint a tab set needs.

nodes.title: Answer every active-state binding from one helper
nodes.why: isActive reads activeTab(), so [class.active], [attr.aria-selected] and @if (isActive(...)) track the same signal and the accessible state cannot lag behind the styling.
nodes.alternative: Toggle only the active CSS class and leave aria-selected and the panels to separate logic.
nodes.tradeoff: The template calls isActive several times per check; the comparison is trivial, and a computed per tab would only add names.

nodes.title: Switch tabs by setting the signal
nodes.why: set replaces the selection; setting the tab that is already active stores an equal value, so the signal does not notify and the open panel stays as it is.
nodes.alternative: Toggle a tab off when it is clicked again, leaving no panel visible.
nodes.tradeoff: Clicking the active tab does nothing, which matches how tab sets behave; a control that can close every section is an accordion.
